issue_context.title: first(), last() list operations on a slice wrongly ignore the slice during aggregation
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
grouped = pl.DataFrame({'key':[123],'value':[456]}).group_by('key')
grouped.agg( pl.col('value').slice(1,2).first() )
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0636b8a-e365-43e5-940f-1294a8174c95)




### Log output

```shell
No output from POLARS_VERBOSE.
```


### Issue description

A slice produces a subsequence and first/last operators should act on the subsequence directly.
This broke for me between 1.12 -> 1.14.
I have checked it is still broken on Google Colab on 1.16.

### Expected behavior

I expect to get a null, matching what 'explode' suggests:

```python
grouped.agg( pl.col('value').slice(1,2) ).explode('value')
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b04a001-29f5-4c9b-86b5-1ab9e336ff42)

I definitely *don't* expect to get a value which has already been filtered by the slice, eg, 456.
